sections.content:
No snake order is solvable. All dead-end. The pegs are too isolated (B7 and E1 are at the ends of the path, and the middle pegs can only shuffle within the B row).
Hmm. So the 1D path model fails too. Let me rethink.
Maybe the goal isn't 1 peg. In level 1, the level cleared when the peg count reached 1. But maybe the level 2 goal is different — for example, "move all pegs to the orange" or "get the pegs to a target position."
Or maybe my understanding of the moves is wrong. Let me look at the level 2 board again:
- 3×7 box, pegs at B2, B3, B5, B7.
- 2×2 box, peg at E1.
- Orange on the path between the boxes.
Wait — maybe the orange is a "peg" that moves, or a special piece: maybe you click the orange and it moves along the path, collecting pegs? Or maybe the orange is the "player" and you move it with arrow keys (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT are valid actions!).
Arrow keys! In level 1 I used UP (t0) and RIGHT (t3) — board_changed was None, N count unchanged. So in level 1 the arrow keys did nothing (or did something invisible). Hmm.
But wait — maybe the arrow keys move the orange! In level 2, the orange is on the path. Maybe you move the orange along the path with the arrow keys, and when it reaches a peg it collects it (removes it)? Goal: collect all pegs (or collect a certain number)?
Let me test: press RIGHT and see if the orange moves. The orange is at roughly rows 30-38, cols 28-38 (center ~ (34, 33)). The path from the orange: right (toward B7) or left (toward D1). Actually the path: the orange connects right to B7 (via the right side), and left to… let me look at the path: from the orange, the path goes right, then up to B7. And from the orange, the path goes left, then down, then right to D1. So the orange has two directions: right (to B7) and left (to D1).
If I press RIGHT, does the orange move toward B7? Let me test.
Actually, first let me reconsider the evidence from the B2 selection: when I selected B2, a g ring appeared around B4 (the jump destination). So the pegs do have jump moves. And B7/E1 have no moves. So the pegs do jump (2D or 1D, same thing here).
If the goal is "1 peg" and it's unsolvable… then the goal must be different. What if the goal is "0 pegs" (collect all pegs into the orange)? Then the orange must be able to collect pegs. How? Maybe when a peg jumps over the orange? Or when the orange moves onto a peg?
Let me test the arrow keys on the orange. If RIGHT moves the orange toward B7, that's a big discovery.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. What if the arrow keys move a selected peg one cell at a time (not jumping)? In level 1, t0: UP did nothing (no peg selected?). t3: RIGHT did nothing. Hmm, but maybe a peg needed to be selected first. t1: MOUSE(19,19) — that's the H1 peg (18,17)! So after t1, the H1 peg was selected. t2: MOUSE(13,12) — a different cell (deselection or probe). t3: RIGHT — nothing happened. So arrow keys on a selected peg did nothing in level 1. OK, so the arrow keys probably don't move pegs.
So what do the arrow keys do? Maybe they move the orange (the "player"). In level 1 there was no orange, so nothing happened. In level 2, the orange exists! Let me test RIGHT.
Let me also test ACTION7 — I don't know what it does. It's in the valid actions. Maybe ACTION7 is "confirm/execute," or something level-specific.
Plan: test RIGHT (see if the orange moves). If the orange moves along the path, the game is: move the orange along the path to collect pegs (or the orange is a mover and pegs are obstacles/targets).
Let me run the probe: action RIGHT, then diff.
